1. What changes
1.1 With effect from 1 September 2026, Supplier Policy POL-SUP-003 §4.4 is replaced by the
following: "A UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if it was issued within the last 12 months, and its
valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the order is placed."
1.2 A certificate that meets the old rule (issued within 24 months and not expired) but not the new one
counts as no certificate for new orders from 1 September 2026. Orders released before that date are not
affected.
2. Why
2.1 In July 2026 a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed our own
incoming abuse test. The cell maker had changed in the meantime. A shorter window, and a margin
before expiry, make sure the certificate describes what the supplier is actually making.
3. What purchase staff must do
3.1 Before raising an order for a lithium-cell part, check the certificate's issue date and its valid-to date
against the new rule.
3.2 The senior buyer runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) on the first working day
of each month with 90 days as the window, and writes to every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate
expires inside it.
3.3 Every other part of POL-SUP-003 §4 stands.
Northbridge Cycles Ltd

| `manual` | the document code | vendor manual or reference (an overview that links to screens, errors and processes) | `man-pur-72` |
| `release` | `rn-` + version | release or patch note, and the 6.x history | `rn-7-2-3-p4`, `rn-7-3-preview` |
| `screen` | `screen-` + screen code | Ledgerline screen | `screen-pur-po-01` |

source that explains it.

## 3. What every page contains

```
---
title, type, slug, summary (one line for the index), audience (staff | hr), sources (raw files),
status (current | superseded | future | mixed), created, updated
---

## Sections                  the facts, grouped as the type needs (see below)

```

   release note that changed system behaviour replaces the older text. Files in `old/` folders, files whose
   status is SUPERSEDED, and older exports are superseded.
3. **E-mails and meeting decisions** from an owner (manager, controller, change board) override a SOP
   until the SOP is reissued; say so and cite both.
4. **The system versus the paper.** When a manual describes behaviour that a later patch changed, say what
   Ledgerline does now (the patch) and that the manual was not updated.
5. Record every case under **Versions and conflicts** as: today's rule, the older or future rule, the
   sources and dates, and the kind (`superseded`, `contradiction`, `future_dated`, `email_overrides_sop`,
   `near_duplicate`, `duplicate`, `rule_not_in_policy`).

## 7. Permissions

Files under `01_policies/HR/CONFIDENTIAL/` are restricted to HR (group NBC-HR-CONF). Facts from them go only
on pages with `audience: hr`, which are listed in `restricted/index.md`, never in `index.md`, and never
linked from staff pages. A staff page may say that a confidential HR document exists and who may read it,
nothing more.

Masters and extracts (item master 2,186 rows, rate contracts 3,226, PR/PO/GRN/AP extracts ~25,000 rows,
400 service definitions) are not copied into the wiki. Each structured file gets one `data-source` page:
what it holds, its sheets and columns, how many rows, how to look a row up (key column), and what it is
for. Entity pages (a supplier, an item family, a cost centre) carry only the rows of their own entity, with
a cell or row reference. To answer "what is the reorder level of X", the reader follows the data-source
page's pointer to the raw sheet.

## 9. Operations

**Ingest** (one source at a time): read the source; write a short source note; decide which pages it
touches (create or update); add its facts with references; record conflicts; append one line to `log.md`:
`## [<timestamp>] ingest | <file> | +<created> ~<updated> | <slugs>`.

**Query**: read `index.md` first; open the pages whose summaries fit; follow `[[links]]`; open the raw source
when a page points to a table or the exact wording matters; answer with citations to raw sources. Say "not
in the documents" when no page or source holds the answer. A good answer may be **filed back** as an
`answer` page, linked from the pages it used, and logged: `## [<ts>] file-back | qa-<slug> | <question>`.

**Lint**: report contradictions between pages or sources, stale or superseded claims stated as current,
future-dated rules stated as current, orphan pages, broken or missing links, uncited claims, and citations
whose quoted text is not found at the cited location. Log: `## [<ts>] lint | <n> findings`.

## 10. `index.md` and `log.md`

`index.md` is the catalogue, read first by every query: one line per page, grouped by type,
`- [[slug]] Title: summary`. It is rebuilt after every ingest. `log.md` is append-only: one line per ingest,
file-back and lint, oldest first, so the wiki's history can be replayed.

UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule (superseded):** From 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3].
* **Older rule:** Under the prior rule, certificates were accepted under a 24-month validity period [^r4]. These certificates count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

AMD-SUP-2026-02 is an amendment to [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] effective 1 September 2026 that tightens the acceptance criteria for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]][^r1][^r2]. Under this amendment, certificates must have been issued within the last 12 months and remain valid for at least 60 days following order placement[^r2]. It governs all new purchase orders placed for lithium-cell parts as of today, 26 October 2026[^r2][^r3].

## Clauses

### 1. What changes
Effective 1 September 2026, [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] §4.4 is replaced such that a [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2]. [Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy · AMD-SUP-2026-02 · v1.0 · effective 2026-09-01]
[Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy › 1. What changes]
1. What changes
1.1 With effect from 1 September 2026, Supplier Policy POL-SUP-003 §4.4 is replaced by the
following: "A UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if it was issued within the last 12 months, and its
valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the order is placed."
1.2 A certificate that meets the old rule (issued within 24 months and not expired) but not the new one
counts as no certificate for new orders from 1 September 2026. Orders released before that date are not
affected.
2. Why
2.1 In July 2026 a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed our own
incoming abuse test. The cell maker had changed in the meantime. A shorter window, and a margin
before expiry, make sure the certificate describes what the supplier is actually making.

[Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy · AMD-SUP-2026-02 · v1.0 · effective 2026-09-01]
[Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy › 3. What purchase staff must do]
3. What purchase staff must do
3.1 Before raising an order for a lithium-cell part, check the certificate's issue date and its valid-to date
against the new rule.
3.2 The senior buyer runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) on the first working day
of each month with 90 days as the window, and writes to every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate
expires inside it.
3.3 Every other part of POL-SUP-003 §4 stands.
